content.title: Just 90 Days Until Ramadan: Are You Ready? 🌙
content.subtitle: Let’s explore how you can prepare yourself over the next 90 days.
content.body:
According to the calendar, only around 90 days remain until Ramadan. Yet it feels like the last Ramadan ended just yesterday. How quickly the days of our lives pass! Think about the people who sat beside you at the iftar or suhoor table last Ramadan. Where are they today?

Perhaps one of them was your father, mother, a family member, or a close friend. They are no longer here. They now rest in the darkness of their graves. Perhaps last year, they too planned to offer more sujood and shed more tears in the coming Ramadan. But that opportunity never returned to them.

Does this question ever cross your mind? Will we live to see the next 90 sunsets and reach the door of Ramadan’s mercy? Or will our names appear on a cold gravestone before it arrives? Are we ready for that inevitable journey?

The Salaf’s Longing: Six Months of Supplication

For our righteous predecessors, Ramadan was not just a yearly ritual. It was a spiritual journey. The renowned Tabi'i Mu'alla ibn al-Fadl (RA) described their deep longing:

“For six months, the Salaf would pray to Allah, asking Him to let them reach Ramadan. Then, for the next six months, they would ask Him with tears to accept their deeds.”

[At-Targhib wat-Tarhib (Imam al-Asfahani), Athar 1753; Lata'if al-Ma'arif (Ibn Rajab), p. 148]

The Prophet’s ﷺ Message to the Companions

During Sha'ban, the Prophet ﷺ would gather his Companions and give them the glad tidings of Ramadan. He said: “Ramadan has come to you, a blessed month. Allah has made fasting during it obligatory upon you...” (Sunan an-Nasa'i: 2106)

He taught us that anyone who wishes to harvest a crop must sow its seeds well in advance.

How Should We Make Dua?

If the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous Salaf were so eager to reach Ramadan, how can we remain careless?

From today, let us make heartfelt dua in every sujood, during Tahajjud, and in our private moments: “O Allah, allow us to reach Ramadan. Grant us good health so that we may witness this blessed month and earn Your pleasure.”

4. How Can You Prepare Over These 90 Days?

  • Make Up Missed Fasts: If you missed any fasts from the previous Ramadan, you must make them up before the next Ramadan. Aisha (RA) would make up her missed fasts during Sha'ban before the arrival of the next Ramadan. (Sahih al-Bukhari: 1950)

  • Make More Dua and Repent: Cleanse your heart through sincere repentance. Do not carry the burden of sins into Ramadan. (Surah An-Nur: 31) Also, make heartfelt dua for the opportunity to reach Ramadan in good health. (Lata'if al-Ma'arif: 148)

  • Build Good Habits: Start practising voluntary fasting and Quran recitation now. This will help you avoid the struggle of starting everything suddenly. The Prophet ﷺ frequently fasted during Sha'ban. (Sahih al-Bukhari: 1969)

  • Plan Your Charity: The Prophet ﷺ was more generous than the blowing wind during Ramadan. (Sahih al-Bukhari: 6) Start preparing mentally and financially to help those in need and earn the rewards of charity.

May Allah Subhanahu Wa Ta'ala forgive us all and envelope us in His embrace of acceptance; grant us longevity to witness Ramadan, and bestow upon us the ability to adorn our lives with sincere devotion to Him. Ameen.
